description:
Quantifies what the HEM assumption costs in the existing converging_diverging_nozzles module versus real non-equilibrium (supersaturated / Wilson-line) condensation.

The four standard benchmark supersonic nozzles are Moore B, Barschdorff, IWSEP and SUT de Laval, with measured axial static pressure distributions and fog-droplet sizes. Primary sources are old conference proceedings (Moore, Walters, Crane & Davidson 1973, IMechE C37/73; Barschdorff 1971; Moses & Stein; Gyarmathy), but digitised geometry and pressure data for all four appear in the OPEN-ACCESS paper 'Numerical analysis of non-equilibrium steam condensing flows in various Laval nozzles and cascades', Eng. Appl. Comput. Fluid Mech.

NOT a pass/fail gate — HEM is expected to miss the condensation shock. The deliverable is the quantified gap, for the paper's V&V section.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 3.4.
title: V&V (diagnostic): wet-steam condensing nozzles — Moore B, Barschdorff

description: Convert the tet volume mesh into a POLYHEDRAL cell mesh via the Voronoi/median dual (one polyhedral cell per input vertex), the equivalent of OpenFOAM polyDualMesh. This yields the polyhedral meshes the reactor CFD needs (better cell quality / lower count than tets). Depends on the tet mesher. V&V: dual of a structured tet block -> valid closed polyhedral cells, each face shared by exactly 2 cells (or 1 boundary), sum(cell vols)==domain volume.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Face-minimal variant landed (commit 834b739): polyhedral_dual_min_faces (dual.rs) — one polygon per primal edge via edge-star walking (interior: closed [faceCentroid,cellCentroid,...] ring; boundary: open fan closed through edge midpoint), ~40% fewer faces than the quad-fan median dual (684 vs 1152 on 4x4x4), verified exact volume + closed + boundary==surface. Resolves the 'not face-minimal' v1 limitation noted at close; quad-fan polyhedral_dual kept as robust fallback.

title: outram-blender: VOLUME MESHING — polyhedral dual mesh (polyDualMesh-style)

description: New workspace crate: a pure-Rust translation of CoolProp (https://github.com/CoolProp/CoolProp, MIT, C++ thermophysical property library — Helmholtz-energy-explicit EOS backend for ~120 pure/pseudo-pure fluids + mixtures, plus incompressibles and humid air). Named with the outram-park-fork- prefix from the start (external-project fork, per the trademark-compliance convention op-ahi). Two hard design constraints from the user: (1) enum dispatch, NOT trait objects, for backend/fluid selection (matches the workspace no-trait-objects rule); (2) hardcode the fluid/EOS data as Rust code -- NO runtime JSON or other file reads (matches njoy's embedded-data philosophy + the workspace static-navigability goal). Verification uses the rfluids crate (https://github.com/portyanikhin/rfluids, a Rust interface to CoolProp) as a DEV-dependency oracle. Book-keeping only; not started.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Crate initiated 2026-07-08: outram-park-fork-coolprop (MIT, workspace member). CoolProp cloned into gitignored reference/. First vertical slice done + verified: Helmholtz engine (Power+Gaussian residual + Lead/LogTau/PlanckEinstein ideal, all derivs), (T,rho) property eval, Water (IAPWS-95) hardcoded (3KB via dev/gen_fluid.py codegen). Water pressure reproduces CoolProp triple-line 611.65 Pa to ~1e-4 at sat liquid+vapor (tests/water_reference.rs). Committed crate 64KB (reference/ 58MB gitignored).
Helium added 2026-07-08 -- verifies to machine precision at its critical point (no non-analytic term). Confirms the Power+Gaussian+ideal engine is exact; Water's ~1e-4 residual is purely the pending non-analytic term (op-kbc.6).

title: outram-park-fork-coolprop — CoolProp thermophysical properties (Rust translation)

description:
`cargo test --release -p outram-mc-libs --doc` fails 2 of 12 doctests:

  test crates/outram-mc-libs/src/geometry/surface.rs - geometry::surface::torus_distance (line 824) ... FAILED
  test crates/outram-mc-libs/src/geometry/surface.rs - geometry::surface::torus_distance (line 829) ... FAILED

CAUSE: the doc comment on `torus_distance` writes its quartic derivation as 4-space-indented prose lines, e.g.

    ///     rho^2(t) + a^2 - b^2 + (b^2/c^2)*ax^2(t)  =  2a*R_perp(t)
    ///     F(t) = G(t)^2 - 4a^2*rho^2(t) = 0.

A 4-space indent inside a /// block is a Markdown indented code block, so rustdoc compiles those math lines as Rust doctests and they fail to parse. They are documentation, not code.

FIX: wrap the derivation in a ```text fence (or ```ignore), matching how the rest of the crate writes non-Rust display math.

PROVENANCE: found 2026-08-06 while verifying bead op-rbo (rng::lcg::init_seed). Confirmed PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to that change — reproduced on develop with the op-rbo edits stashed (baseline: 9 passed / 2 failed; with the op-rbo fix: 10 passed / 2 failed, the extra pass being a new init_seed doctest). Not fixed there to keep that change scoped to the RNG.

NOTE: `cargo test --lib --tests` does not run doctests, which is why this has gone unnoticed.
title: outram-mc-libs: 2 pre-existing doctest failures in geometry::surface::torus_distance
